requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`. I read `yaml.rs#const[KINDS]` only to see how the profile is built. Expected behaviour comes from the requirement text.

**Mapping obligations to tests**
- **Block mapping entries as `pair`, named by the written key.**
  - `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` in `src/outline/tests.rs` parses `a: 1` and `"b":`.
  - It asserts `pair[a]` and `pair["b"]`, so the quoted key is kept as written.
  - It also asserts line spans for each node.
- **Flow mapping entries as `pair`.** The same test parses `c: {d: 1}` and asserts `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d]` on its own line.
- **Block sequence entries as anonymous `item`.** The same test parses `- f: 1` and `- 2` under `e:`. It asserts two `item@` nodes, one per entry, each with the right span. This covers both an item that contains a pair and a scalar item.
- **Nesting beneath the nearest enclosing item.** The same test asserts the full path chain `pair["b"]/pair[e]/item@/pair[f]`.
- **Selected source ends at the last non-comment token.**
  - `yaml_selection_ends_before_trailing_comment_tokens` in `tests/outline_content.rs` selects `pair[key]` from `key: value # trailing comment`.
  - It asserts the text is `key: value` and the span is `0..10`.
  - It also checks that `pair[a]` in `a:\n  b: 1\n# before next\nd: 2` stops at `b: 1`, so a following standalone comment is excluded.
  - It checks that the nested `pair[a]/pair[b]` selects `b: 1`.
- **Comment ownership.** The requirement cites `requirements.references.outline_comments` and does not restate it. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` still checks that a comment before `second:` is owned by `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`, not by the previous key. `no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds` also checks that YAML sequences and plain scalars produce no invented fallback kinds.
- **Selectors, percent encoding and duplicate suffixes.** These are cited from `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. They are reviewed under that requirement and need no test here.

**Possible gap, not reported.** There is no test that flow sequence entries do not become `item`s. The requirement lists only block sequence entries, and the profile maps only `block_sequence_item` to `item`. I did not treat this as a gap, because the requirement text does not explicitly name that case.

**Result.** Each stated obligation has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome. I found no unacknowledged gap.

The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
